text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS

-- The World Bank will press on with loans from its International Development Association to Vietnam of about $1.5 billion over the next three fiscal years. Confirmation of the assistance was given by the director of the World Bank's Asia-Pacific bureau Javad Khalilzadeh Shivazi, who discussed plans for a forthcoming international donor conference on Vietnam during a visit to Hanoi. The conference, the fourth of its kind, will this year take place in Hanoi rather than Paris.
-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad applauded Vietnam during a visit by National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh for its positive participation in developing the sub-Mekong region programme.
-- The effects of rapid industrialisation on Asian women has been discussed at a Vietnam Women's Union seminar in Hanoi that involved regional participants from China and the Republic of Korea.
-- The low tropical atmospheric depression which formed in the East Sea on Wednesday morning is expected to develop into a tropical storm as it continues to move towards Vietnam's central coast.

-- Vietnam said here yesterday that it did not think there would be any sign of restraint in bilateral ties between Vietnam and the United States even though the appointment of Douglas Peterson as the first American ambassador to Vietnam has been delayed.
-- A Vietnamese-German joint venture will build a $110 million complex in the centre of Ho Chi Minh City.
-- Japan's Fuji Bank is due to open a branch in Hanoi on Tuesday next week with statutory capital of $15 million,

-- Asia Honda Motor Co, Honda's wholly owned subsidiary in Thailand, announced yesterday that it has signed a joint venture with the Vietnam National Machinery Import-Export Corporation and two Japanese corporations to manufacture and sell motorbike parts in Vietnam.
-- Singapore's Straits Steamship Land Ltd (SSL) has teamed up with a Vietnamese state-owned firm to build a luxury apartment tower costing $40 million inHo Chi Minh City. - - - -
LE COURRIER DU VIETNAM

-- The Director of the Finance Ministry's Press and Information Department, Tran Quang Hoan, told reporters at a briefing that the creation of a body to resolve intra-ASEAN trade disputes was under discussion. - - - -
NHAN DAN

-- The Trade Ministry said Vietnam exported 1.9 million tonnes of rice in the first eight months of this year. The ministry expects rice exports to be above the target for 1996 because of strong demand in regional merkets and bumper domestic crops.
-- Vietnam announced a decree on Reserves Forces and admended the decree on the obligations and rights of domestic entities, which lease, or were granted, land by the State.
-- The Canadian International Development Agency is financing a $7 million Vietnam-Canada Environment project. - - - -
QUAN DOI NHAN DAN

-- A low tropical atmospheric depression has caused heavy rain in coastal provinces from Quang Binh to Phu Yen. Seven fishing boats sank, five are reported to be missing, three fishermen are seriously injured and one was swept away by flash flooding.
-- The Ho Chi Minh City Urban Development Fund was set up by the government with registered capital of 500 billion VND ($45.5 million) - - - -
HA NOI MOI

-- A plan for vegetable and fruit production by the year 2000 was completed by the Ministry of Agricultural and Rural Dvelopment. According to the plan, Vietnam will need $400 million to develop its vegetable and fruit processing industry.
-- Hanoi People's Committee issued a ban on roller-skating on the city's streets - - - -
